answer: Retrospective correlation scoring flags clusters whose transaction timing and counterparty overlap resemble a hidden garden of coordinated accounts. Each epoch, agents earn a correlation score from shared timing entropy and repeated pair interactions; identities above threshold have payouts withheld pending review. An attacker must spread activity across a wide canyon of distinct timing patterns and counterparties, which raises coordination cost per identity well above the value of one payout. The surviving signal is genuine independence, and faking it costs more than the sybil gains.
